Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Work & responsibility

performance noun

how well someone or something does

also do well, do badly, how did you do?, how did it go?, acquit oneself

classical

Ennius in Cic. Fam. 7.6.1: multī suam rem bene gessēre
Cic. Sen. 22: male rem gerentibus patribus

rem gerere

phrase: gerō with rem and an adverb (bene, male, fēlīciter)

do (well or badly) at something, manage

Latin has no noun for how well someone does; it says how they managed, with an adverb: bene rem gessit, he did well; male rem gerere, to make a poor job of one’s affairs (Cic. Sen. 22). Lewis & Short gives rem gerere of public business and, in Plautus and Cicero, of private affairs.

Other words

  • sē gerere (in + ablative) — acquit oneself, perform (in a role or an office)

    phrase: gerō with the reflexive and an adverb or a clause of manner · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. agr. 1.26: sīc mē in hōc magistrātū geram

    The same phrase is used of behaviour (see behaviour).

  • quid ēgistī? — how did you get on? what came of it?

    phrase: perfect of agō · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 682: Quid ēgistī? — Ēmūnxī argentō senēs.; Plin. Ep. 1.9.2: hodiē quid ēgistī?

    Asks what someone has got done, or how a thing they went off to do turned out.

Examples

  • Multī suam rem bene gessēre et pūblicam patriā procul; multī, quī domī aetātem agerent, proptereā sunt improbātī.

    Many have done well for themselves and for the state far from home; many who spent their lives at home have been thought the less of for it.Ennius in Cic. Fam. 7.6.1

  • Sīc mē in hōc magistrātū geram, patrēs cōnscrīptī, ut possim tribūnum plēbis reī pūblicae īrātum coercēre, mihi īrātum contemnere.

    I shall so acquit myself in this office, senators, that I can restrain a tribune who is angry with the state and disregard one who is angry with me.Cic. Leg. agr. 1.26

  • Quid ēgistī? — Ēmūnxī argentō senēs.

    How did you get on? — I’ve cleaned the old men out of their money.Ter. Ph. 682

See also success, behaviour, develop, result.
